coworkers.name: A
coworkers.about: Neurotic corporate believer. Competent and helpful; cares far too much.
coworkers.opening: Good morning! Our customer score target today is 94.2 percent. I believe in us.

lines.text: Did you offer {name} lamination? Attach rate is a KPI.
Quick check: did {name} get the lamination pitch? It's on the scorecard.
Yes! That's an attach! I'm logging it.
Love that. That's shareholder value, right there.
Okay. That's fine. That's totally fine. The attach rate is just a number.
No, sure. I'll just note it as a missed opportunity. For us. As a team.
Corporate says every interaction is a brand moment. Even this one.
Our net promoter score is up two tenths this quarter. I printed the chart.
Remember: we don't sell copies. We sell outcomes.
Shareholder value starts at the counter. I read that in the onboarding deck.
If you see a smile, that's a five-star review in waiting.
One of our core values is Ownership. I own this stapler.
Break in {minutes} minutes. Not that I'm counting. I am counting.
Our numbers are dipping. Is it me? It's probably me.
The manager looked at the dashboard and sighed. I heard it from the back.
Processing. Efficiently.
Order in, order out. That's throughput.
Caught one! Order #{job}: they asked for {field}. I fixed it before it printed. You're welcome! Teamwork!
I re-sorted the pickup shelf by due date. It's more intuitive. You'll love it.
Jam cleared! Uptime is a value.
Taking my fifteen. Fourteen and a half, actually.
I'm back. I used the time to reflect on our goals.
Great shift, team! Same time tomorrow? Please say yes.
I color-coded the break schedule. Green means rest. Rest is a deliverable.
If we hit 95 percent today, regional sends a pizza. One pizza. For the region.
Pro tip: say 'absolutely' instead of 'yes.' It tests better.
I read the employee handbook again last night. For fun. Chapter four is a page-turner.
Every jammed printer is just an uptime opportunity.
I set three goals for today. Two are about synergy. One is about lunch.
Customer delight is up. I can feel it. I can't prove it.
Corporate says we're a family. A family with quarterly targets.
Did {name} hear about our premium cardstock? Asking for the dashboard.

coworkers.name: Brody
coworkers.about: The one you don't want. Slow, needs help, never gets in trouble.
coworkers.lore: The owner's son. That's why he still works here: he can't be fired, and the manager knows better than to try.
coworkers.opening: Oh. Hey. You know how to do the printer stuff, right? Cool.

lines.text: Yo. How do I do labels again?
Hey, the computer's asking me a question. Can you look?
Which box is the medium one? They all look like boxes.
Is cardstock the thick one or the shiny one?
This customer wants something. Can you talk to them?
How do you make the copier do two sides?
Oh nice. Yeah. I knew that.
Cool, cool. You're good at this. You should be a manager.
Okay. I'll just do it my way.
Wow. Fine. I'll figure it out.
So I kind of messed up order #{job}. It's fine. You can fix it, right?
My dad says this place is a learning opportunity.
Do we get paid for breaks? Asking for me.
I'm thinking about getting into crypto. Or podcasts.
I don't really do mornings. Or afternoons.
Working on it. Kind of.
This takes forever, right? Is it supposed to?
The printer made a noise and stopped. I didn't touch it. I touched it a little.
The copier was like that when I got here. Like, two minutes ago.
I unplugged the card reader to charge my phone. Is that bad?
I restarted the router. It was slow. Now it's slower.
I sat on the box pile. Some of them are flat now.
Gonna grab something from the back. Brb.
I'm back. There was a thing. Don't worry about it.
I'm taking my break. My other break.
Okay. I'm back. Mentally, mostly.
Peace. Tell my dad I was here.
Is it Friday? It feels like it should be Friday.
My dad says I have a natural talent for leadership. I think he's right.
I'm on my phone but I'm listening. Mostly.
This shirt was like three hundred dollars. Don't get toner on it.
I told my dad we should get a smoothie machine in here. He's thinking about it.
Do you ever just stand here and think about stuff? Same.
My trainer says I need more rest days. Today's one of them.
Where do the bags go? Like, the paper ones.
The register is beeping at me. Why is it beeping at me?
Can you watch my station? I have to take a call. It's personal.
How many staples is a stack? Like, roughly.
So I kind of broke something on the computer. It's fine. You can fix it, right?
I clicked a thing on the computer and now it looks different. Can you fix it?

coworkers.name: C
coworkers.about: The talker. Fine at the job; exhausting to be near.
coworkers.opening: Okay, so you will not believe what happened at my cousin's thing last night.

lines.text: Right? Can you believe that? Right?
Okay but what would YOU have done?
Wait, are you listening? This is the good part.
THANK you. Finally someone gets it.
See, you get it. Okay, so then...
Mm-hm, right, exactly. Anyway.
I SAID, can you BELIEVE that?
HELLO? I'm telling a STORY.
Did I tell you about my neighbor's ferret? He has opinions.
I'm doing a juice cleanse. Day one. It's going badly.
My horoscope said today would be a lot. It's a lot.
Have you ever thought about how weird staples are? Little metal hugs.
A made a laminated vision board. For this job. It has a mission statement.
A asked the manager for feedback. On purpose. Who does that?
Brody's dad owns the place, you know. That's why he's still here.
Brody once took a ninety minute break. The manager said good hustle.
Oh my gosh, I love your bag. Where's it from? Tell me everything.
Is that for a party? I love parties. Okay so last weekend...
Okay so anyway, where was I.
Multitasking. That's my love language.
Taking my break. I'll tell you how it goes.
Okay I'm back and you will NOT believe the line at the coffee place.
Bye! Text me! Actually don't, I'll text you.
My sister's getting married. Again. Third time. I'm a bridesmaid. Again.
I had the weirdest dream. You were in it. You were a stapler.
Okay so my landlord texted me a thumbs up. Just a thumbs up. What does that mean?
I'm starting a podcast. It's about podcasts.
I can't believe it's only noon. Is it noon? It feels like noon.
Do you like mushrooms? I have a whole thing about mushrooms.
I think the guy at the coffee place likes me. He spelled my name right.
You'd never do that, right? Tell me you'd never do that.
Be honest. Was I wrong? I wasn't wrong.

story: So my cousin's wedding. The DJ shows up dressed as a pirate. Nobody asked for a pirate.
The pirate DJ only plays sea shanties. My aunt is furious. My uncle is dancing.
Then the cake arrives and it's shaped like a ship. They planned the pirate. Nobody told me.
Plot twist: the pirate DJ is my cousin's ex. From high school. He wore the hat back then too.
My cousin cries, the ex cries, the cake leans. Somebody says it's a sign.
They get back together. Not the bride. The ex and my aunt. I'm not joking.
So now my aunt is dating a pirate DJ and the family group chat is on fire.
Update: they're opening a sea shanty food truck. I've been asked to invest. I have eleven dollars.
The food truck launched. It's called Shanty Snacks. The fries are shaped like anchors.
Shanty Snacks got a health inspection. They passed. The inspector requested a shanty.
My cousin and the bride are fine, by the way. They went on a cruise. Ironic.
Anyway. That's the story. Ask me about my neighbor's ferret sometime.
